performers: Orquestra de música antiga de l’Esmuc; Alba Roca, concertmaster and director
question: What changes when the bass drops out of a dance built around its pulse?
intro: This instrumental dance comes near the end of The Fairy Queen. A triple pulse supports changing string figures, but the bass does not play continuously: its withdrawal creates one of the dance’s strongest contrasts.

cues.title: Three beats under dotted figures
cues.text: The bass gives the dance a steady three-beat foundation while the upper strings use long-short dotted figures. Listen for how the accented shape of the tune sits over that regular lower movement.
cues.evidence: The inspected Chaconne score is in 3/4 with four string staves, dotted upper figures and repeated crotchets in the bass: https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/6/69/IMSLP435506-PMLP237007-Suite_from_The_Fairy_Queen_Complete.pdf, PDF page 50, printed page 48.

cues.title: Dance inside a spoken play
cues.text: The Fairy Queen was first performed in London in 1692. Its spoken adaptation of A Midsummer Night’s Dream surrounds separate musical entertainments; this instrumental chaconne is a dance from Act V, not a sung setting of Shakespeare’s dialogue.
cues.evidence: The work catalogue identifies the 1692 premiere, anonymous Shakespeare adaptation and Act V Chaconne: https://imslp.org/wiki/The_Fairy_Queen,_Z.629_(Purcell,_Henry).

cues.title: No continuous bass ground
cues.text: The basso rests through this upper-string passage. That absence is a useful correction to the idea that every chaconne must repeat an unchanged bass without interruption: here the texture itself becomes part of the variation.
cues.evidence: The score has basso rests in bars 49–64, while the three upper parts continue. The report shows markedly lower level from about 1:10 through 1:45, and a strong change near 1:08: https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/6/69/IMSLP435506-PMLP237007-Suite_from_The_Fairy_Queen_Complete.pdf, printed pages 50–51.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Church, court and theatre
cues.text: Purcell became organist of Westminster Abbey in 1679 and composed for major royal occasions as well as the theatre. His music for the stage belongs beside, not instead of, that continuing institutional career.
cues.evidence: Westminster Abbey documents the 1679 appointment and music for the 1685 and 1689 coronations and Queen Mary’s funeral: https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/commemorations/henry-purcell-family.

cues.title: Recorded in a museum
cues.text: This performance was recorded in Barcelona’s Museu de la Música on 7 April 2018. The source credits Marc Urrutia for sound recording using an ORTF microphone arrangement, and Alba Roca as concertmaster and director.
cues.evidence: The ESMUC Commons description explicitly gives the date, Sala de teclats at Museu de la Música, Marc Urrutia and ORTF: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Purcell_TheFairyQueen_ActV_Chaconne_Z629_Esmuc.flac.

transitions.title: The pulse remains while the tune moves faster
transitions.how: After the opening dotted phrases, the upper strings take up running figures. The bass retains a more regular tread, so the change in rhythmic density happens above a continuing foundation rather than through a new metre.
transitions.evidence: The notation changes its upper-string figures at bar 17 while retaining 3/4 and moving bass crotchets. The report marks 0:24, consistent with the opening phrase group’s proportion: https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/6/69/IMSLP435506-PMLP237007-Suite_from_The_Fairy_Queen_Complete.pdf, printed page 48.

transitions.title: The basso stops and the upper voices answer
transitions.how: The full four-part passage closes, then the bass rests. The upper strings continue with separated figures and staggered activity. Removing the lowest line lightens the texture without stopping the triple-time dance.
transitions.evidence: Basso rests begin at bar 49 in the inspected score. The report has a strong change near 1:08 and a pronounced level reduction immediately afterwards: https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/6/69/IMSLP435506-PMLP237007-Suite_from_The_Fairy_Queen_Complete.pdf, printed page 50.

transitions.title: The low part rejoins in stages
transitions.how: The bass returns after its extended rest, first supporting the upper strings with short notes and intervening silences. The fuller texture is therefore rebuilt through punctuation rather than a new uninterrupted ground at once.
transitions.evidence: The score’s bar 65 restores the basso, followed by intermittent notes and rests. The report changes at 1:32 and then gradually recovers level before 1:54; the time is approximate: https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/6/69/IMSLP435506-PMLP237007-Suite_from_The_Fairy_Queen_Complete.pdf, printed page 51.

transitions.title: Active bass restores the fuller dance
transitions.how: The lower part becomes more continuous and the string lines take up a fuller range of moving figures. The restored bass weight connects this closing span to the earlier four-part dance without requiring a literal repeat of its entire opening.
transitions.evidence: The later score, approximately bars 78 onward, restores extended moving bass patterns. The report’s strong change at 1:54 begins the louder closing region. The material letter is distinct because no complete thematic return is claimed: https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/6/69/IMSLP435506-PMLP237007-Suite_from_The_Fairy_Queen_Complete.pdf, printed pages 51–53.

source.title: Purcell, The Fairy Queen — instrumental suite, Bart Dunn typesetting after Shedlock
source.locator: Chaconne, printed pages 48–53, four original string parts. The cello desk represents written Basso, not a documented inventory of the recording’s bass instruments; no keyboard realization is asserted.

timeline.note: Four-part string dance; the written Basso supplies the foundation.
Basso rests in bars 49–64; the three upper parts continue.
The Basso rejoins intermittently, with rests between short contributions.
The later dance restores more continuous bass movement beneath the upper strings.
